reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its normed additive group structure, a measurable space structure whose sigma-algebra is the Borel sigma-algebra, and a second-countable topology, every everywhere differentiable function f:E->R, all real eta,beta,B satisfying eta>0, beta>=0, B>0 and the global bound ||gradient f(x)-gradient f(y)||<=beta||x-y|| for all x,y in E, and every x0,xp in E, the following holds. Put g=gradient f(xp), h=x0-eta*g, P=Law(sqrt(eta)*G) and q=Law(h+sqrt(eta)*G), where G has the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability law on E. Put U=Lebesgue measure restricted to (0,1] and nu=U product P. Define C=integral_E f(h+z) dP(z)-<g,h>. For x in E and (t,z) in R x E define W(x,(t,z))=<(pi/2)*(cos(pi*t/2)*(x-h)-sin(pi*t/2)*z),g-gradient f(h+sin(pi*t/2)*(x-h)+cos(pi*t/2)*z)>, Wc(x,(t,z))=min(B,max(-B,W(x,(t,z)))), m(x)=integral_(R x E) Wc(x,v) dnu(v), and Z=integral_E exp(m(x)) dq(x). Inner products and scalar multiplications in these formulas are real. Define the one-trial law Lambda=q product (Poisson(2B) product (nu^N product V)), where V is Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,1] and nu^N is the countably infinite iid product indexed by the natural numbers starting at zero. Thus a trial p=(X,K,S,A) draws independently X with law q, K with Poisson law of rate 2B, an iid sequence S_i=(T_i,Z_i) with law nu, and A uniformly on [0,1]. Let H be the measurable acceptance condition A<=product_(i=0)^(K-1) ((B+Wc(X,S_i))/(2B)), with empty product 1 when K=0. Let rho=Lambda^N be the law of an iid sequence omega of complete trials. Define F(omega) to be the X coordinate of trial omega(n) at the least natural index n for which omega(n) satisfies H, if such an index exists, and define F(omega)=x0 otherwise. Then nu and q are probability measures; W and Wc are measurable on E x (R x E), and m is measurable on E. For every x in E, each of v->W(x,v), v->Wc(x,v), and v->max(|W(x,v)|-B,0) is Bochner integrable with respect to nu; |m(x)|<=B; and |m(x)-(<g,x>-f(x)+C)|<=integral_(R x E) max(|W(x,v)|-B,0) dnu(v). The function x->exp(m(x)) is integrable with respect to q, and exp(-B)<=Z<=exp(B). The output map F is measurable, and its pushforward of rho equals the normalized exponential tilt of q by m, namely the probability measure with density exp(m(x))/Z with respect to q. The rho-measure of the event that every trial fails H is zero. The one-trial acceptance probability is Lambda(H)=exp(-B)*Z and is at least exp(-2B); these equalities and bounds are expressed in the theorem in extended nonnegative reals using ENNReal.ofReal. If K_n is the K coordinate of omega(n), define the extended nonnegative total count L(omega)=sum_(n=0)^infinity 1_{every i<n fails H} K_n. This count includes K_n for the successful trial as well as for every preceding failed trial, and on a never-accepting sequence it sums all trial counts. Its extended nonnegative integral under rho equals (ENNReal.ofReal(exp(-B)*Z))^(-1)*ENNReal.ofReal(2B) and is at most ENNReal.ofReal(2B*exp(2B)). Here the inverse and multiplication are those of extended nonnegative reals. These cost conclusions concern the sum of the Poisson counts, rather than a separately defined wall-clock, function-evaluation, or gradient-evaluation cost. The output distribution conclusion is explicitly the tilt by the clipped mean m; no equality of that distribution with the tilt by <g,x>-f(x)+C, no distributional error bound for that latter tilt, and no explicit beta- or dimension-dependent estimate for the displayed clipping-tail integral are stated. The integral defining C is a typed signed integral; integrability of z->f(h+z) under P is not separately asserted in the displayed conclusion.
